description: A straight, north–south trending, low‐relief embankment or causeway approximately 280 m long and 4–6 m wide. On the DTM slope map it shows a subtle, linear convex ridge with <1° slope contrast. The curvature derivative highlights it as a small positive ridge, and hillshade reveals a faint shadow line. In the NIR band there is a narrow, darker tone along the ridge axis, indicative of higher moisture retention or organic‐rich soil (‘dark earth’). The feature is not coincident with any mapped modern road or trail on OpenStreetMap.

A rectilinear raised‐field platform, roughly 120 m by 60 m, aligned east–west. On the slope derivative it appears as a flat plateau set 0.8–1.2 m above surrounding terrain. Curvature highlights a convex margin on its northern and southern edges. In the NIR image the platform interior registers a uniform, darker signature compared to adjacent forest, suggesting enriched anthropogenic soil or moisture‐retentive fill. No modern parcel boundaries or infrastructure coincide with this footprint.
